$comment: SOURCE, NOT GENERATED. How a release reads on the changelog, shaped after Preline's (Zafar, 17 Sep 2026, pointing at preline.co/docs/changelog.html): a title, then chips (an icon and a label, like Preline's "New Components & Improvements" and "Fixes and Improvements"), each followed by its items with a bold lead ("People:", "Layout:") and the drawings the item is about. His asks on the way: "topic > icons, topic > icons. not all topics first and then all icons after that", "categorize them, not just text > icons. titles, etc.", "redrawns deserve to be a separate topic, not within a topic and each subtitle must carry shareable link like the main titles". So redraws are always their own chip. Per version: `title` (the release's headline, which every version has, released ones included, because the page heads each entry by it) and optionally `sections`: chips with `title`, `icon` (a drawing from this set, by name) or `logo` (a platform's own mark, for a chip about that platform, where a drawing of ours would stand in for someone else's trademark: `react`, drawn from components/brand-logos.tsx), `text`, and items in `sections` with `title`, `text`, `names` (added), `redraws` or `removed` (drawings the release took out of the set, since 1.6.0 retired `cloud-minus`: the generator reads them off the two trees, so a name listed here only places one, it never claims one). A version with no `sections` is drawn with default chips, New drawings and Redrawn, straight off git. pipeline/build-history.mjs gives every chip and item an `anchor` (v<version>-<chip>, v<version>-<chip>-<item>) that the site links, keeps only the drawings the entry carries, and appends anything no item claims in a last untitled group, reported, so a stale list never drops a drawing. Keyed by the version the work ships as, so nothing is re-keyed at the tag. Numbers go in as {names} and {files}. Anything in backticks is set as code, on the page and the Paper board both, the way a post sets an icon name. Where a version has sections they replace the note.

sections.title: Pointers
sections.text: The pointer is drawn again in all four directions, and its fill carries the finger lines.

sections.title: Files
sections.text: The file fills cut their folded corner clear of the edge, and the paperclip runs longer.

sections.title: Charts
sections.text: In two-tone the charts grey their axes and keep the data in black.

sections.title: Media
sections.text: The gallery frames take a tighter radius, and play is smaller.

sections.title: Actions
sections.text: The three dots are larger, and the sparkle's tips reach the same 2-unit margin as everything else.

sections.title: Shapes
sections.text: The dice take larger pips, and in two-tone circle-progress-play greys the part still to play.

sections.title: Web
sections.text: In two-tone globe-off greys its far side.
